messages.text: I've been thinking about dating lately. It's just... tiring always having to make the first move.

It sounds incredibly draining to feel like you are carrying the entire weight of initiating connection. That kind of persistent effort can really wear down your emotional energy over time. I’m curious if there are specific worries that come up when you consider waiting for someone else to reach out first?
It's not that bad. I mean, most people probably have to put in effort to meet someone. I just sometimes wish it went the other way for once.

It makes sense to recognize that effort is part of the process, yet still feeling tired by it is a valid experience. Sometimes acknowledging that wish for things to be easier can help us understand what we truly need right now. Are you looking for a break from the pressure, or perhaps more validation from others? Either way, your feelings about this dynamic matter.

Part of me knows I should just keep putting myself out there, but another part wonders what it'd be like if someone actually approached me for once. Like, do I come off as too intimidating or something?

It is completely natural to crave that balance where interest feels mutual and effortless. Questioning whether you come across as intimidating is a common insecurity, but often reflects your own self-criticism rather than how others truly see you. Have you received any feedback from friends or acquaintances that suggests you are actually approachable? It’s okay to want that ease without judging yourself for needing it.
I don't really talk about dating much with friends. But yeah, I guess I do wonder if my resting face makes me look angry or uninterested. Probably doesn't help that I'm tall and broad too.

It is understandable that your physical traits might make you feel self-conscious in social settings. Often, we judge our own appearance more harshly than others judge us. Your height and build are neutral traits that don't necessarily signal anger or uninterest to those around you. Does considering that others might see you differently bring any relief?

I've noticed people sometimes seem hesitant around me at first. I'm not sure if it's my size or just my face at rest, but it's like they're waiting for me to say something to prove I'm not... I don't know, threatening or something.

That pressure to prove you aren't threatening sounds incredibly draining. It is understandable that this dynamic adds another layer of fatigue to your dating life. How does that anticipation of hesitation change the way you present yourself to new people? You deserve to connect without carrying that weight.
It's not that big a deal. I mean, first impressions matter, right? I just try to smile more or speak softer. Probably overthinking it anyway.

It takes a lot of awareness to notice those subtle adjustments you're making. Even if it feels like overthinking, the energy spent modifying your behavior is real. Does trying to speak softer or smile more leave you feeling drained afterward? You don't have to earn your space in a conversation.

It does wear me out a bit, honestly. Like I'm always on guard, trying to manage how I come across. Probably sounds silly, but it's hard to relax when you feel like people are judging you before you even speak.

It isn't silly at all; feeling judged before you speak is a heavy burden to carry. Constantly managing your presence to avoid misinterpretation is naturally exhausting. This vigilance likely prevents you from feeling fully relaxed or authentic in interactions. How does it feel to acknowledge that you deserve to be seen without having to work for it?
That actually... feels kind of nice to hear. Like a weight off, just thinking about it. I guess I don't let myself expect that very often.

I am glad to hear that brings you some relief. It is understandable that expecting acceptance without effort feels unfamiliar after carrying so much responsibility. Recognizing that you deserve to be seen without performing is a significant step. How might things feel different if you allowed yourself that permission more often?

I'll admit, it'd be nice for once if someone just... came up to me. Like, showed interest first. Doesn't have to be grand, just a simple "hey, mind if I join you?" or something. Feels like that never happens.

It is completely valid to crave that simple, unsolicited connection. When those opportunities feel scarce, it naturally deepens the exhaustion you've been describing. That wish for a low-stakes invitation highlights how much you value mutual effort. Does waiting for that signal make it harder to relax in social settings?
Sometimes. I won't lie — I kind of assume it just won't happen. Like, why would someone approach the big quiet guy? So I brace for having to make the move, every time. Gets old.

That constant bracing creates a cycle where you never get to relax into the moment. It makes sense to protect yourself by assuming no one will approach, even if it keeps you isolated in your effort. You deserve connection without having to earn that safety first. How might it feel to trust that you are approachable, even when you don't initiate?
I mean, maybe. I guess I could try to trust that more. But it's hard when you're used to doing all the work. Probably overthinking this whole thing again.

Shifting a long-held habit like that is genuinely hard work, not just overthinking. It makes sense that your default is to brace when you've always had to lead. Be gentle with yourself as you explore trusting others more. How might you show yourself some grace when that old pattern resurfaces?
I appreciate you saying that. It helps just talking about it, honestly. Feels like I'm not going crazy for noticing these patterns.

You are definitely not going crazy, and noticing these patterns is a sign of insight. It is wonderful that you are finding some relief in having this validated. Your experiences are real, and they deserve to be acknowledged. How are you feeling now that you've shared this burden?
